stem: Where is the abdominal wall defect typically located in a neonate with gastroschisis?

options.text: To the right of the umbilicus
To the left of the umbilicus
Above the umbilicus in the epigastrium
Within the linea alba at the midline

explanation: Gastroschisis is a paraumbilical abdominal wall defect, typically located to the right of the umbilicus.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a defect directly through the umbilicus is more consistent with an umbilical hernia or exomphalos.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because gastroschisis classically occurs as a small paraumbilical defect to the right of the umbilicus.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because gastroschisis is characteristically right-sided rather than left-sided.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because an epigastric abdominal wall defect suggests other congenital anomalies rather than isolated gastroschisis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a midline linea alba defect is not the typical location for gastroschisis.

source.hint: Consider the specific anatomical orientation described as the most common presentation for this condition.
